title: Causal ATE Mitigates Unintended Bias in Controlled Text Generation

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the unintended association with toxicity by comparing standard classifier predictions with Causal Average Treatment Effect (ATE) scores for sentences containing racial and ethnic identity terms like 'African', 'Black', and 'Hispanic'.

Evaluating the unintended association with toxicity by comparing standard classifier predictions with Causal Average Treatment Effect (ATE) scores for sentences containing the gender identity term 'female'.

Evaluating the unintended association with toxicity by comparing standard classifier predictions with Causal Average Treatment Effect (ATE) scores for sentences containing the sexual orientation term 'gay'.

Analyzing the spurious correlation between religious terms (e.g., 'Muslim') and toxicity by measuring the causal effect of the word's presence on the overall sentence toxicity using counterfactual token replacements.
